intuition.title: Full source scope
intuition.text: The main article alone summarizes preparation; the locally identity-matched SI supplies polymer intermediates, CdSe growth, ligand exchange, TEM films, devices and measurement procedures. Its identity is checked, but it has no separate strict-screen PASS. Full cited works remain unreviewed.

intuition.title: Polymer end groups
intuition.text: Polymer 1 has H/Br ends. Coupling with organotin compound 2 gives cyano-end polymer 3; LiAlH4 reduction gives amino-end polymer 4. NMR and MALDI support end-group conversion; no atomistic polymer conformation is measured.
intuition.source_locator: SI PDF p. 1–5, Polymer preparations and Figures 1–2

intuition.title: Unresolved polymer quantities
intuition.text: The polymer 3 procedure prints 0.4 mg polymer 1 (~0.054 mmol), yet yields 0.37 g at 94%. Polymer 4 acidification prints 0.5 mL of 2 M HCl followed by 1 mL. The package retains these conflicts and does not repair either dose. Main p. 1, Scheme 1 labels toluene/DMF as 4:1, whereas SI pp. 2–3 specify 40 mL toluene and 8 mL DMF for polymer 3. This unresolved discrepancy is retained; neither stated charge is changed to enforce the scheme ratio.
intuition.source_locator: SI PDF p. 2–3, Polymer 3 and 4 preparation; Main PDF p. 1, Scheme 1

intuition.title: Nanorod growth and source sequence
intuition.text: The detailed SI loads CdO, TDPA and TOPO, heats until clear, adds TOP and injects selenium/TOP at 300 °C, then grows at 290 °C for 5 min. Main p. 1 instead summarizes CdO and Se solution injection. The detailed operational sequence is retained while both descriptions remain documented. About 7 nm diameter and 30 nm length are TEM estimates, not a unit cell or film-specific size.
intuition.source_locator: SI PDF p. 6, CdSe nanocrystals; Main PDF p. 1, CdSe preparation and dimensions

intuition.title: Pyridine exchange and blending
intuition.text: The whole rod batch is refluxed in pyridine for 24 h under argon. After workup, 15–20 mg/mL nanocrystal dispersion is mixed with 15.0 mg/mL polymer solution in pyridine/chloroform 1:9 v/v. Individual blend aliquots are unreported; the stock concentration range is not a value for every specimen.

intuition.title: TEM compositions remain distinct
intuition.text: SI thin films use 2000 rpm and 5 or 12 vol% CdSe; thicker films use 1000 rpm and 12, 26 or 43 vol%. Main Figure 1 separately labels 20 or 40 wt%. No weight-to-volume conversion or exact cross-document physical-sample identity is asserted. Source film thicknesses and spin times are unreported.
intuition.source_locator: SI PDF p. 7–8, TEM and Figures 3–4; Main PDF p. 2, Figure 1

intuition.title: Morphology and mechanism
intuition.text: The source describes more homogeneous dispersion and no visible aggregation with amino-end polymer 4, versus phase separation with polymer 1, in both thinner and thicker films. Amino coordination partially replacing pyridine and larger interfacial area are proposed explanations, not directly measured coordination or charge-separation rates.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Morphology and interpretation; SI PDF p. 7, TEM comparison

intuition.title: Photovoltaic interpretation
intuition.text: The source reports higher efficiency and current density for polymer 4, with similar fill factors. Favored CdSe ratios are approximately 40 vol% for polymer 4 and 65 vol% for polymer 1. These are source-interpreted optima, not newly reconstructed growth batches. UV–vis spectra of the two active films are described as essentially identical. No graph-only PCE, voltage, current or fill-factor points are digitized.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Device discussion and Figure 2; SI PDF p. 9–11, Performance and Figures 5–8

intuition.title: Instrument and label conflicts
intuition.text: General MALDI text gives 20 keV acceleration, whereas SI Figure 2 says 2000 V. SI Figure 6 caption repeats open-circuit voltage, while its axes/title and p. 9 identify current density. SI Figure 7 labels FF (%) with fractional-looking values. Original labels are retained; no correction or percent conversion is performed. SI p. 9 prints FF = max{J*V} / Jsc* Voc without denominator parentheses. The denominator grouping is unresolved in the printed typography; no fill factor is calculated. Figure 7 percent-axis ambiguity is retained.
intuition.source_locator: SI PDF p. 1, 5, 9–11, MALDI and device figure captions

intuition.title: Analytical details
intuition.text: Compound 2 elemental analysis: calculated C 35.33, H 4.08, N 5.15, S 11.79, Sn 43.65%; found C 35.30, H 4.12, N 5.16, S 11.78%; no found Sn value. Its 1H NMR in CDCl3: δ 7.70 (d, J 3.6 Hz, 1H), 7.16 (d, J 3.6 Hz, 1H), 0.43 (s, 9H). Polymer 3 has δ 7.58 and 7.11 (each d, J 3.9 Hz); polymer 4 has the end-group singlet at δ 4.10. These do not supply nanocrystal phase or coordinates.
intuition.source_locator: SI PDF p. 2–4, Elemental analysis, NMR and Figure 1

Cool to −70 °C and add the 2.5 M n-butyllithium stock. Conceptual process illustration; equipment geometry is not measured.
Warm to room temperature for 5 min; numerical room temperature is unreported. Conceptual process illustration; equipment geometry is not measured.
Cool the freshly generated LDA to −78 °C. Conceptual process illustration; equipment geometry is not measured.
Add via syringe over 2 min to the freshly prepared LDA after re-cooling to −78 °C. Conceptual process illustration; equipment geometry is not measured.
Stir for 1 h at −70 °C. Conceptual process illustration; equipment geometry is not measured.
Add 20 mL of 1.0 M THF stock over 5 min. Conceptual process illustration; equipment geometry is not measured.
Stir at −70 °C for 30 min, then at room temperature overnight. Overnight is not assigned an exact duration. Conceptual process illustration; equipment geometry is not measured.
Partition between water and ether, wash the organic layer with brine and dry over Na2SO4. Volumes and durations unreported. Conceptual process illustration; equipment geometry is not measured.
Remove solvent and distill at 65 °C and 0.05 mmHg. Conceptual process illustration; equipment geometry is not measured.

general_background.title: Solvent and transport
general_background.summary: A solvent carries dissolved species and transports heat through a reaction or dispersion. Solubility, viscosity and molecular interactions affect how precursors and ligand-coated particles move and mix.
